text:
maya: Quick question — we're finalizing GCP Cloud KMS guidance for Redwood Private deploys. Customers ask what exact service account perms and key layout we need, plus best practice for envelope encryption and key rotation. Anyone have a short checklist we can share?

liam: Short answer: give the runtime service account the minimum KMS role on the specific CryptoKey (or key ring) it uses. Prefer `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for datakey ops.

rohit: A couple of practical options: 1) Per-customer key rings in the customer's project (recommended for isolation), or 2) Central key project with per-customer keys (easier to manage for ops). Tradeoffs: isolation vs. central control.

maya: If we go per-customer, do we need the SA in the customer project or just grant cross-project perms?

sarah: You can keep the SA in the customer project (common) or in our central project and grant it access cross-project. For Private deployments running in a customer VPC, we recommend creating a dedicated SA in the same project as the KMS key and granting only `cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`. Avoid `roles/cloudkms.admin` unless ops needs key management.

rohit: Example IAM binding command we include in the docs: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding my-encryption-key \n  --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-private \n  --member="serviceAccount:redwood-private-sa@CUSTOMER_PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \n  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
```
Also ensure `cloudkms.googleapis.com` is enabled for the project: 
```
gcloud services enable cloudkms.googleapis.com --project=CUSTOMER_PROJECT
```

maya: Good. What about envelope encryption and the flow we should implement? We want the runtime to store only encrypted data keys, not plaintext keys.

liam: Envelope encryption flow (high-level): runtime generates a random data key locally -> use it to encrypt payloads (or disk volumes) -> call KMS to encrypt the data key (Decrypt only when necessary). Store the encrypted data key alongside the ciphertext. For backups/state you never store plaintext.

sarah: This also helps with rotation: when a key is rotated you rewrap data keys (decrypt with old key version and re-encrypt with new version) or maintain multiple key versions and do lazy rewrap on read/write. Document both: immediate rewrap vs lazy rewrap.

rohit: For rotation, we generally recommend: enable automatic rotation on the CryptoKey with a rotation period (e.g., 90d) and implement rewrap logic on write. Example to set rotation: 
```
gcloud kms keys update my-encryption-key \n  --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-private \n  --rotation-period=7776000s --next-rotation-time=2025-06-01T00:00:00Z
```
Note: automated rewrap is app responsibility — KMS rotates the primitive but you must re-encrypt stored data keys with new version if you want forward protection.

maya: Any gotchas about key versions vs creating new keys?

sarah: Use CryptoKey versions for rotation within the same logical key. Creating a new CryptoKey is a heavier change and requires updating config references. Versions let you keep the same key name and rotate transparently. If you need to revoke all previous versions, you can disable older versions.

rohit: Also: check location. Keep key ring location in same region as the workload/storage (e.g., `us-central1`) to avoid cross-region latency and egress. If customer requires multi-region keys, document the tradeoffs.

maya: Audit logging — what should we tell customers to enable so they can track decrypt/encrypt operations?

liam: Enable Data Access audit logs for Cloud KMS (these are not on by default for all services). Send audit logs to a secure Logging sink, export to a BigQuery dataset or Cloud Storage for retention. Recommend retention policy and SOC review.

rohit: Sample note for docs: "Enable ADMIN_ACTIVITY and DATA_ACCESS audit logs for the KMS resource; export to a locked BigQuery dataset and ship access logs to Security team." Also add an alert for unusual `cryptoKeyVersions.use` counts.

maya: If a customer wants zero-downtime key rotation, what's the pattern?

sarah: Dual-wrap approach: write new data wrapped with the new key version while still accepting reads using older wrapped keys. On read, if data key is wrapped by an old version, you can rewrap and rewrite behind the scenes. That gives near-zero downtime.

rohit: A simple operational fallback: keep a fallback key in a separate key ring/region and update runtime routing policy for emergency decrypts. But document strict audit & approvals if used.

maya: Anything about Workload Identity / SA impersonation we should caution?

liam: If using GKE/Workload Identity or similar, prefer workload identity pools and short-lived tokens. Grant the IAM role to the KSA mapped SA, not to broad groups. Avoid long-lived JSON keys.

kms-bot: [system] KMS API quota reminders: encrypt/decrypt quotas are per-project; high-throughput workloads should request quota increase early.

maya: Awesome — can someone draft a short checklist blurb for the install guide? I'll paste it in the Private deploy quickstart.

sarah: I'll draft. Checklist: enable KMS API, create key ring, create CryptoKey (set rotation), create dedicated SA, grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on the CryptoKey, export audit logs, ensure region alignment. Keep it <10 lines.

maya: Perfect — thanks all :thumbsup:
